rows.t: The first paragraph of the Replace dialog (its second paragraph, about page numbers, is kept). The old file is deleted from storage once the new one is saved (`document/document.service.ts:285`, `replaceDocumentFile`), so the swap cannot be undone: consequence, then permanence (C11). Comments, summaries and citations point at the document, which stays (`document.controller.ts:356`). The em dash becomes a clause and the curly quotes straight ones (C5).

rows.m: and its files stop appearing for students
rows.t: When the dialog is for a material (the next row is a file). Deleting a material archives it (`material.service.ts:73`): it leaves the staff list too (`listForStaff` skips archived materials, `:96`) and no screen restores it, so the body says it is removed from the list and cannot be undone, and keeps the sentence that chat history is kept. The curly quotes become straight (C5). The claim that chat history is kept is the source's own, and it holds: `MaterialService.delete` only sets the material's lifecycle to ARCHIVED (`material.service.ts:73-84`), and the tables that hold chat history, `UserInteraction` and `Conversation` (`schema.prisma:108` and `:161`), have no relation to a material or a document, so nothing cascades to them.

rows.o: “{fileName}” is removed permanently, along with its annotations and everything the tutor learned from it.
rows.n: "{fileName}" is deleted, along with its comments, its summaries, the search index Kiwi built from it and the stored file. Chats that cited it keep their answers. You can't undo this.
rows.m: is removed permanently, along with its annotations
rows.t: When the dialog is for a file (the previous row is a material). The delete removes exactly these, in one transaction and then the stored file: the document's comments, summaries and embeddings (the search index) and its row (`common/database/document.service.ts:73-80`), then the file in storage (`document/document.service.ts:1094-1120`). Chats keep their answers: an interaction holds only a `pdfId` string, no foreign key (`prisma/schema.prisma:121`), and the delete touches no interaction. "Annotations" and "everything the tutor learned" said less than the code does (C16), and "permanently" becomes "You can't undo this", the sentence A-14.24 and A-14.25 use (C11, C8).
